content.question: Methane contributes to global warming, so it is called what?
content.note:
Methane ($CH_4$) is a potent Greenhouse Gas.
It is much more effective at trapping heat than $CO_2$ over a short time frame. Sources: Common sources include wetlands, livestock (enteric fermentation), and rice paddies.

content.question: Which wind is also known as the 'Snow Eater'?
content.note:
The Chinook is a warm, dry wind that blows down the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains in North America.
It can raise temperatures rapidly in winter, melting snow in hours, hence the name 'Snow Eater'.

content.question: On which date is the Summer Solstice observed in the Northern Hemisphere?
content.note:
The Summer Solstice occurs on June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.
On this day, the North Pole is tilted closest to the Sun, and the Sun is directly over the Tropic of Cancer. Result: It is the longest day of the year in the north.

content.question: What causes the cycle of day and night on Earth?
content.note:
The Rotation of the Earth on its axis once every 24 hours causes Day and Night.
One half of the Earth faces the Sun (day) while the other faces away (night).
Note: Earth rotates from West to East, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the East.

content.question: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
content.note:
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
It is so big that all other planets could fit inside it twice.
Note: It is a Gas Giant and is famous for its Great Red Spot, a giant storm.

content.question: What is the scientific study of rocks, concerning their composition, texture, formation, distribution, and the physical-chemical conditions of their origin, called?
content.note:
Petrology is the branch of geology that studies rocks.
It examines how rocks are formed (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic). Etymology: The word comes from the Greek 'petra' meaning rock and 'logos' meaning study.

content.question: The imaginary lines that connect places of equal elevation at regular intervals are called what?
content.note:
Contour Lines are used on maps to show terrain.
All points on a single contour line are at the same height above sea level. Rule: When lines are close together, it indicates a steep slope; when far apart, it's a gentle slope.

content.question: A special type of well in which water rises to the surface automatically through a hole due to pressure is called what?
content.note:
An Artesian Well is a well that doesn't require a pump.
The water is under enough natural pressure to rise to the surface. Condition: It occurs when an aquifer is trapped between two impermeable layers of rock.

content.question: What causes ocean tides?
content.answer: The gravitational pull of the Sun and the Moon on the Earth.
content.note:
Tides are caused by the Gravitational Pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun.
The Moon's pull creates a 'bulge' in the ocean water. Types: Spring Tides (highest) occur during full/new moon, and Neap Tides (lowest) occur during the moon's quarter phases.

content.question: The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass in India located south of which river?
content.note:
The Deccan Plateau is the large plateau in southern India.
It lies south of the Narmada River and is bounded by the Satpura range to the north and the Ghats to the east and west.
Note: It is mostly made of volcanic basalt.

content.question: Which water body separates the Andaman Islands in the north from the Nicobar Islands in the south?
content.note:
The Ten Degree Channel is a channel that lies on the 10-degree latitude line.
it separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.
Note: It is about 150 km wide.

content.question: The Sunda Strait is located between which two places?
content.note:
The Sunda Strait is the strait between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra.
It connects the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean.
Note: The famous volcano Krakatoa is located in this strait.

content.question: How much time does the Earth take to rotate 1°?
content.note:
The Earth takes 4 minutes to rotate 1°.
Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours ($24 \times 60 = 1440$ minutes). So, $1440 / 360 = 4$ minutes. Application: This is why there is a 2-hour time difference between Gujarat and Arunachal Pradesh (roughly 30° difference).

content.question: What are the reference lines called that connect the North Pole to the South Pole?
content.note:
Longitudes (or Meridians) are imaginary vertical lines.
They measure how far East or West a place is from the Prime Meridian.
Note: Unlike latitudes, longitudes are not parallel; they all meet at the poles.

content.question: A canal watercourse where water is forcefully lifted and made to flow against the natural slope of the land is called what?
content.answer: Lift Channel or Lift Irrigation System.
content.note:
In a Lift Irrigation System, water is not transported by natural flow.
It is mechanically lifted using pumps to reach higher elevations. Use: This is common in plateau regions where rivers flow much lower than the agricultural fields.

content.question: Over time, a meander loop gets cut off from the river and forms a lake, which is called what?
content.note:
An Ox-Bow Lake starts as a curve, or meander, in a river.
Erosion and deposition eventually cut the neck of the meander, leaving a U-shaped body of water. Location: These are common in the mature stage of rivers in flat plains.

content.question: Which list by the IUCN provides detailed information on endangered species of flora and fauna?
content.note:
The Red List is published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
It is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species. Categories: Species are categorized from 'Least Concern' to 'Extinct'.

content.question: The temperate grasslands of South Africa are called what?
content.note:
The temperate grasslands of South Africa are known as the Velds.
They are divided into Highveld and Lowveld based on altitude.
Note: Maize (corn) is the most important crop grown here.

content.question: The large bends in a river are called what?
content.note:
Meanders are loop-like bends in a river.
They form because of erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank of a river.
Note: Over time, meanders migrate across the floodplain.

content.question: Which is the first state in India to receive rain from the Southwest Monsoon?
content.note:
Kerala is the first state to be hit by the Southwest Monsoon.
The monsoon usually arrives at the Kerala coast around June 1st.
Note: This marks the beginning of the rainy season for most of India.

content.question: An area reserved for wildlife where cultivation, grazing, forestry, and human interference are prohibited is called what?
content.note:
A National Park is an area strictly reserved for the betterment of wildlife & biodiversity.
Unlike Wildlife Sanctuaries, human activities like grazing and private ownership are strictly prohibited here. Authority: They are established under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.

content.question: When all ecosystems in a geographic area come together to form one large unit (the largest ecosystem on Earth), it is called what?
content.note:
A Biome is a large naturally occurring community of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat.
It is the largest level of ecological organization. Examples: Tundra, Taiga, Desert, and Tropical Rainforest.

content.question: In the first phase of the action plan for the introduction of the Cheetah in India, in September 2022, which animals were released in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh?
content.note:
Cheetahs were reintroduced to Kuno National Park from Namibia.
The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952.
Note: This is the world's first intercontinental translocation project for a large carnivore.

content.question: Which concept was proposed by Hutchinson in 1957 to describe the relationship of an individual or a population with all aspects of its environment?
content.note:
The Ecological Niche is the specific role or position of a species within an ecosystem.
It describes how an organism responds to the distribution of resources and competitors. Analogy: If the habitat is the organism's 'address', the niche is its 'profession'.

content.question: El Nino is a phenomenon in which, every 2 to 5 years, a warm ocean current replaces the cold current along the coast of which country?
content.note:
El Niño involves the warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific.
It weakens the trade winds and affects global weather, often causing droughts in India and heavy rain in Peru. Frequency: It occurs irregularly every 2 to 7 years.

content.question: What was the main objective of the Montreal Protocol?
content.note:
The Montreal Protocol (1987) was designed to phase out the production of substances responsible for Ozone depletion (like CFCs).
It is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties.
Note: The ozone layer protects Earth from harmful UV radiation.

content.question: The first meeting of the Kyoto Protocol, an international treaty to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, was held in which country?
content.note:
The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in Kyoto, Japan in 1997.
It was an international agreement to reduce Greenhouse Gas emissions to fight global warming.
Note: It operated on the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'.

content.question: In which year did the Kyoto Protocol come into effect?
content.note:
The Kyoto Protocol legally came into effect in 2005.
It required ratification by enough countries to account for 55% of global emissions.
Note: It has since been largely succeeded by the Paris Agreement.

content.question: The Moon takes approximately how many days to complete one orbit around the Earth?
content.note:
The Moon orbits the Earth once every 27.3 days.
This is its Sideral period.
Note: Because the Earth is also moving, it takes slightly longer (29.5 days) to see the same phase again (New Moon to New Moon).

content.question: What type of rocks were once igneous or sedimentary but have been transformed by intense heat and/or pressure within the Earth's crust?
content.note:
Quartzite is a non-foliated Metamorphic Rock.
It forms when Quartz Sandstone is subjected to high heat and pressure. Characteristics: It is extremely hard and resistant to chemical weathering.

content.question: Which planet has the highest number of moons/satellites?
content.note:
Saturn has the highest number of discovered moons, totaling 146.
It recently overtook Jupiter in the moon count.
Note: Its largest moon, Titan, is the only moon in the solar system with a thick atmosphere.

content.question: The canal channel where water flows due to the force of gravity is called what?
content.note:
In a Gravity Canal, the water flows naturally from a higher elevation to a lower one.
No pumping is required because the alignment follows the natural slope of the land.
Note: This is the most cost-effective type of irrigation canal.

content.question: Mawsynram receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world because the monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal collide with which hills?
content.note:
Mawsynram (in Meghalaya) is the wettest place on Earth.
The Khasi Hills act as a funnel, forcing the moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal to rise and cool rapidly, resulting in extreme rain. Nearby: Cherrapunji holds many historical rainfall records as well.
